name: Amanda Sorensen

five_sec.what_is_it: Plan to Eat. The recipe organizer I already trialed.
five_sec.who_for: People who have a recipe collection and like building plans.
five_sec.trust_why: 4.8 App Store and 4.7 Google Play right on the hero, and 'no card required' is honest. It's a real product, just not for me.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Hero says 'Recipes, Meal Plans and Grocery Lists, All in One App.' It's an app.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Same reason as last time. 'Save, Organize, Plan, Shop' means I do the saving, organizing and planning. That's the part I don't have time for.
full_page.whats_missing: Done-for-you plans. Per-person food rules, like dairy-free for me only.

PTE.quote: I already did the 14 days. 'Keep all your recipes in one place' assumes I have recipes. I have a 3-year-old who eats four foods.

five_sec.what_is_it: Weekly meal plans, I think. The headline is just 'Less Stress, More Dinners.'
five_sec.who_for: Families with young kids, going by the video.
five_sec.trust_why: Feels like an established brand, but the first screen is a video and a cartoon, no specifics.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The 'How It Works' drawing is a phone surrounded by food. Not sure if it's a box or a list until step 2.

full_page.what_stopped_me: A pop-up asking for my email before anything else, and no price on the page. Also no way to say 'dairy-free for mom, regular for the toddler.'
full_page.whats_missing: A dairy-free option that doesn't change the whole family's menu. A price. Whether the trial needs a card.

EM.quote: Fifteen plans and one is Plant Based, but there's no 'dairy-free for mom, regular for the 3-year-old.' I'd be picking the whole family's diet around me.

five_sec.what_is_it: HelloFresh meal kit, with a pop-up game.
five_sec.who_for: People who want boxes of food shipped.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer!' is a slot machine. And the button behind it is greyed out.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The pop-up is literally green HelloFresh boxes, and food bowls behind it.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Price is behind a zip code, the fine print ties '10 Free Meals' to the 4-person, 5-recipe plan, and I'd still have to cook at 6:15 with a baby.
full_page.whats_missing: A price per week. Dairy-free filtering for one person.

HF.quote: Open a box to reveal my offer, then the fine print says '10 Free Meals' needs the 4-person, 5-recipe plan. Hard pass, respectfully.

five_sec.what_is_it: An app that decides dinner for you.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Trusted by 90,000+ families' and a polished phone mock-up. But the button is 'Letter from the CEO,' which is odd.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's an app screen called 'Your Menu.' Looks like planning, not shipping.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The meal page says 'prices are available when you download the app.' Then the pricing page: $25 a month for 150 messages. Also AI writes the recipes, so does it remember dairy-free every single time?
full_page.whats_missing: How dietary rules work, per person or per household. A straight price on the meals page.

OL.quote: 'IT TAKES THE THINKING OUT' is literally my life, but $25 a month for 150 messages? For dinner? Oof.

five_sec.what_is_it: Plans five dinners, texts the family to vote, and fills my Instacart or Walmart cart.
five_sec.who_for: Families with kids, people who order groceries online.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Powered by Instacart' and the plain 'We don't deliver food' line. Small company though.
five_sec.next_step: 'See a sample week,' then check diet options.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Bold line under the hero: 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: Nothing big. I had to dig: dairy-free for the whole family is on Free ('dietary needs... respected on every plan'), but a profile per person with allergies is a Family feature. At least it says so.
full_page.whats_missing: A screenshot of the per-person profile on the home page. Target and Cub named alongside Wegmans and Aldi (Target is in the Instacart list, Cub isn't).

DD.quote: 'Just your email. No password, no card.' I can do that between stops. But does my dairy rule stay just mine after day 14? That's Family, so, $4.99.

dd_offer.why: Says it several times: 14 days of Family, no card, then add a card from Account to keep it or go back to Free. The 3-day email warning is a nice touch.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: I'm back on the free plan. Plans and the cart still work, but the per-person profiles, texting and reminders stop unless I add a card. Nothing gets charged.

head_to_head.reason: Done-for-you plans I can set up on the train with just an email, and it tells me outright that per-person food rules are on Family.

EM.reason: Per-person rules instead of picking one diet plan for the whole house.

PTE.reason: No recipe library to build. That's why I quit Plan to Eat.

OL.reason: $4.99 versus $25, and DinnerDrop doesn't hide the price until I download.

HF.reason: No gamified pop-up, and it fills the Instacart cart I already use.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page, 'What you get' section: add a phone screenshot of one person's profile with 'Dairy-free (just Mom)' and one sentence saying which diet settings are on Free and which need Family.
